changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance-led buyers, replace the study claim with an offer: Send us one month of your statements and we'll price what manual matching costs you, covering the hours, your own staff cost, and write-offs from deposits you never matched. The point is that it's your number, not ours.
changes.why: The deal went from "Dead, honestly. I had it at 20 percent." to signed when Wen priced the problem from one month of the customer's statements and staff costs, and the CFO valued it because "that's my number, not yours."

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For buyers where finance owns the evaluation (for example, a distributor selling in three states), open with: Know where every deposit came from, and close the month without a week of archaeology. Then go straight to the payout-to-transaction-to-ERP matching in M9.
changes.why: The global, every-currency opener got silence from a buyer selling in three states. The CFO framed the problem as "month-end is a week of archaeology." and "I just want to know where my money is.", talked about "the deposits" rather than payments, and reconciliation was the only thing that drew a reaction.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For distributors and wholesalers, don't lead with retail or software customer stories. Offer a reference call with another distributor once we have one, and until then lean on the prospect's own business case rather than generic stories.
changes.why: The CFO asked to talk to another distributor and dismissed the retail story with "this is a company that sells sweaters." We never got her that call, and she brought it up twice before signing.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: For accounts whose IT team is small and not building anything, stop leading with developer messaging on the first call. Keep APIs, docs and sandbox for a later technical review if the IT contact asks.
changes.why: The standard first-call deck was run on an IT team of "four people and they aren't building anything," so the developer pitch had no one to land with.
